lessons.title: 1. True/False & The `and` Operator
lessons.description: Booleans represent truth values: `True` or `False`. The `and` operator returns `True` only when BOTH conditions are `True`. Implement `can_drive(has_license, is_sober)`.
learning_objectives: Use boolean values and the `and` operator
lessons.solution_code:
def can_drive(has_license, is_sober):
    return has_license and is_sober

tests.name: test_can_drive
tests.unittest_code:
def test_can_drive(self):
    self.assertTrue(can_drive(True, True))
    self.assertFalse(can_drive(True, False))
    self.assertFalse(can_drive(False, True))

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 6.11 Boolean Operations — and, or, not (Language Reference)

lessons.title: 2. The `or` & `not` Operators
lessons.description: The `or` operator returns `True` if AT LEAST ONE condition is `True`. The `not` operator flips `True` to `False` and vice versa.
lessons.solution_code:
def can_enter_club(has_vip_pass, is_on_guestlist):
    return has_vip_pass or is_on_guestlist

tests.name: test_can_enter_club

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 6.11 Boolean Operations — and, or, not (Language Reference)

exercises.question:
What does this program print?

```python
def can_enter_club(has_vip_pass, is_on_guestlist):
    return has_vip_pass or is_on_guestlist

print(can_enter_club(False, True), can_enter_club(False, False), not can_enter_club(True, False))
```
exercises.explanation: `or` is True when at least one side is True, so (False, True) gives True and (False, False) gives False; `not` then flips the third call, which was True, to False. The other options are what `and` instead of `or`, or dropping the `not`, would print.

lessons.title: 3. Ghost Gobble Arcade Game
lessons.description: Pac-Man may eat a ghost only while the power pellet is active AND he is touching a ghost. Implement eat_ghost(power_pellet_active, touching_ghost) so it returns True exactly when both inputs are True (all four combinations are tested).
learning_objectives: Combine and, or, and not to model game logic
lessons.solution_code:
def eat_ghost(power_pellet_active, touching_ghost):
    return power_pellet_active and touching_ghost

tests.name: test_ghost_gets_eaten
tests.description: eat_ghost is True only when both inputs are True.
tests.unittest_code:
def test_ghost_gets_eaten(self):
    self.assertEqual(eat_ghost(True, True), True)
    self.assertEqual(eat_ghost(True, False), False)
    self.assertEqual(eat_ghost(False, True), False)
    self.assertEqual(eat_ghost(False, False), False)

lessons.title: 4. Security System Access (Practice)
lessons.description: Implement unlock_door(has_keycard, passcode_correct, is_emergency): the door opens when the emergency override is active, OR when the keycard is held AND the passcode is correct. Every combination listed in the tests must hold.
learning_objectives: Apply boolean logic to access security problems
lessons.solution_code:
def unlock_door(has_keycard, passcode_correct, is_emergency):
    return is_emergency or (has_keycard and passcode_correct)

tests.name: test_unlock_door
tests.description: Emergency override or keycard+passcode opens the door.
tests.unittest_code:
def test_unlock_door(self):
    self.assertTrue(unlock_door(False, False, True))
    self.assertTrue(unlock_door(True, True, False))
    self.assertFalse(unlock_door(True, False, False))
    self.assertFalse(unlock_door(False, True, False))
    self.assertFalse(unlock_door(False, False, False))

sublessons.title: Select the combinations that open the door

exercises.question: The rule is: the door opens when the emergency override is active, OR when the keycard is held AND the passcode is correct. Select every combination that opens the door. (keycard, passcode, emergency)
options: no keycard, no passcode, emergency active
no keycard, correct passcode, emergency active
no keycard, no passcode, no emergency
correct_answer: no keycard, no passcode, emergency active
no keycard, correct passcode, emergency active
exercises.explanation: Emergency alone opens the door whatever else is true; without it, both the keycard and the correct passcode are needed.

lessons.title: 5. Section 2 Checkpoint: Control Flow Mastery
lessons.description: A camera device can take a photo only when it has a working camera module AND its memory is not full. Implement can_take_photo(has_camera, memory_full) — all four input combinations are tested.
lessons.solution_code:
def can_take_photo(has_camera, memory_full):
    return has_camera and not memory_full

tests.name: test_can_take_photo
tests.description: Photo allowed only with a camera and free memory.
tests.unittest_code:
def test_can_take_photo(self):
    self.assertTrue(can_take_photo(True, False))
    self.assertFalse(can_take_photo(True, True))
    self.assertFalse(can_take_photo(False, False))
    self.assertFalse(can_take_photo(False, True))
